response.rationale: Acute severe upper GI bleeding in a 1-year-old with negative H. pylori, normal liver function/coagulation, and no CT-identifiable bleeding source, plus persistent hemoglobin drop, best fits a vascular anomaly requiring early endoscopy.

rejected.why: No liver disease or portal hypertension; normal liver function tests make gastroesophageal varices unlikely.
No retching/forceful vomiting history and persistent severe anemia are atypical for Mallory-Weiss tear.
Variceal hemorrhage is contradicted by normal liver function tests and lack of portal hypertension evidence.
Gastritis can cause hematemesis, but absence of NSAIDs/H. pylori and ongoing severe bleeding despite acid suppression make a focal vascular source more likely.
Peptic ulcer disease is unlikely with negative H. pylori, normal gastrin, and no NSAID exposure.
